attempts.label: DANDI:000115
attempts.entry_title: Hippocampal replay and the eight-arm goal task (Gillespie et al. 2021)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Gillespie et al. (2021) on dandiset 000115, which holds the raw CA1 tetrode broadband, port events, position and task logs of four rats in an eight-arm win-stay lose-switch task. Trials, goal blocks and reward rates are rebuilt from the task logs and checked against the hardware events. The replay findings need ripples and a clusterless decoder run on about 9.1 TB of raw data, which the dandiset holds in no reduced form.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Gillespie et al. (2021) from dandiset 000115

outcomes.statement: The analysis includes 24, 32, 23 and 33 behavioural sessions and 89, 85, 105 and 166 trial blocks for the four subjects.
outcomes.source: Figure 1D and 1E-F legends
outcomes.quote: n = 24, 32, 23, and 33 sessions per subject, respectively ... n = 89, 85, 105, and 166 trial blocks per subject, respectively
outcomes.notes: Re-run after the two questions were answered. With the first valid trial after each goal change in the old block, all eight counts are within 10% under both session readings. Sessions are 25, 32, 24 and 33 against 24, 32, 23 and 33. Blocks with a trial of task phase 4 or more are 88 for jaq against 89 under reading (a) (day 6 epochs 2 and 5 left out), 85 against 85 for roquefort, 109 against 105 for despereaux and 166 against 166 for montague. Under reading (b), day 6 epoch 4 is the only jaq session with fewer than eight arms visited, so it is the second excluded session; the first (fewer than 75% decoded on the same segment) cannot be found without the decoder, so each of the other 26 jaq sessions was tried, giving 88 to 93 jaq blocks, all 26 within tolerance (91 with day 6 epoch 2). Measured values are reading (a), the first the criterion lists. What the answers changed. The closing-trial answer moves montague from 167 blocks (the old-goal-visit reading, which the earlier record reported as its measured value) to 166 and leaves the other subjects unchanged; over all 116 run epochs, of the first trials after a goal change, 383 visit the old goal, 35 another arm unrewarded and 5 the new goal with a reward, all 5 counted in the old block as the claims file says. The session answer adds the search over the poorly decoded session under (b); before, (b) was day 6 epochs 2 and 4 only. The outcome is unchanged (reproduced). With no session excluded (a variant), jaq has 27 sessions, outside tolerance, and 96 blocks. The files hold one more run epoch for jaq and for despereaux than the paper counts, and which one cannot be told; leaving out any one more under reading (a) gives 24 and 23 sessions and 82 to 87 jaq blocks and 100 to 108 despereaux blocks, all within tolerance. All run epochs are the goal_delay task, and none uses forage assist: forageNum is 1 in the 111 logs whose header states it, and no log, the five without a header included, names more than one arm in a CURRENTGOAL line. The DIO beam breaks confirm that arm 6 was never entered in jaq day 6 epoch 4, also after its last logged trial; it is the only jaq session with fewer than eight arms in the log or in the DIO.
deviations: Trials are rebuilt from the StateScript logs in the files (port entries, the printed goal, reward and timeout lines), not from the paper's preprocessed trial structures; rewards match the DIO pump onsets in 115 of 116 epochs.

Under session reading (b), the session with fewer than 75% of movement frames decoded on the same segment cannot be identified without decoding, which is blocked; every candidate is run and all give the same outcome.
Session selection by decode quality (the code's gooddecode) cannot be applied without decoding; all run epochs are counted, less the two excluded for jaq.

outcomes.statement: Aligned to the goal change, the outer-arm reward rate starts at chance (0.125) and rises; aligned to the first reward at the new goal, it is well above chance, so all subjects keep visiting a goal once found.
outcomes.source: Results, Rats learn to perform a flexible spatial memory task, paragraph 5; Figure 1E and 1F
outcomes.quote: Aligned to the first search trial of each trial block, the reward rate at the outer arms for all subjects began at chance (0.125) and rose (Figure 1E) ... the outer reward rate was well above chance, indicating that all subjects preferentially visited the goal location consistently after finding it (Figure 1F)
outcomes.notes: Re-run after the two questions on fig1d-sessions-blocks were answered, with blocks closed by the first valid trial after each goal change (the closing trial dropped) and sessions under reading (a) and under reading (b) for each of the 26 candidates for jaq's poorly decoded session. In all four subjects, the reward rate on the first trial after the goal change is 0.065 to 0.133 with its lower S.E.M. bound at or below 0.125 (0.039 to 0.106). It rises to 0.584 to 0.710 by trial 15, with bands not overlapping trial 1 and Spearman rho 0.943 to 0.993 (largest p 1.4e-7, montague). After the first reward at the new goal every point of trials 1 to 15 has its band above 0.125 (lowest lower bound 0.234, roquefort). Blocks are 88, 85, 109 and 166 under reading (a). What the answers changed. The closing-trial rule, against the old-goal-visit reading, moves roquefort's trial 15 from 0.597 to 0.584 and its Spearman rho from 0.985 to 0.979, despereaux's rho from 0.996 to 0.979 and its lowest Figure 1F bound from 0.420 to 0.429, montague's rho from 0.950 to 0.943, and under reading (b) (day 6 epochs 2 and 4) jaq's trial 15 from 0.696 to 0.681 and its rho from 0.993 to 0.975; it leaves every condition holding; the session answer adds the candidates under (b) (jaq trial 1 0.065 to 0.080, trial 15 0.662 to 0.710, lowest Figure 1F bound 0.420 to 0.453). The outcome is unchanged (reproduced). Jaq (0.068) and roquefort (0.094) start below chance on trial 1, not at it, which the criterion's "or lies below" allows. The plain reading of "rises" (trial 15 above trial 1) holds in every subject too. The per-trial values (p, S.E.M., n for trials 1 to 15) are printed for each subject.
deviations: Trials are rebuilt from the StateScript logs, as for fig1d-sessions-blocks, with the same session readings.
The criterion's "rises" is judged as trial 15 above trial 1 with non-overlapping S.E.M. bands and a positive Spearman correlation of rate with trial number; both are printed.

outcomes.statement: SWRs occur mainly during reward consumption at the home port, the center ports and the rewarded goal arm, and are rarely detected at unrewarded outer ports.
outcomes.source: Results, Most SWRs contain interpretable spatial content, paragraph 1; Supplementary Figure 1C
outcomes.quote: SWRs occurred primarily during reward consumption (Supplementary Figure 1C) ... As expected, SWRs were rarely detected at non-goal outer arm ports, which did not provide reward
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds only the raw 30 kHz broadband of 128 channels, about 9.1 TB over 57 files stored one channel per chunk, and no spikes, LFP, ripple times, linearised position or decoder output. The notebook measures 8.8 MB/s when streaming it (data check), at which one 90-minute run epoch takes 79 minutes and the whole dandiset 288 hours, far beyond the 30-minute limit, before any spike detection or decoding. The claim needs ripples detected on the raw broadband across the CA1 cell-layer tetrodes. The electrode table also gives every channel's location as None, so the CA1 cell-layer tetrodes and the corpus callosum reference tetrode the Methods use cannot be identified.

outcomes.statement: During movement the decoded position (posterior maximum) is usually on the same or an adjacent maze segment as the real position, and the median deviation between them is less than one 5 cm bin, on every maze segment.
outcomes.source: Results, Most SWRs contain interpretable spatial content, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 3A-C; Methods, Spatial decoding, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: The median deviation between predicted and real position was less than a single spatial bin (5 cm), indicating that the maximum of the posterior and the subject's real position most often corresponded to the same spatial bin, and this was consistent across all segments of the maze
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds only the raw 30 kHz broadband of 128 channels, about 9.1 TB over 57 files stored one channel per chunk, and no spikes, LFP, ripple times, linearised position or decoder output. The notebook measures 8.8 MB/s when streaming it (data check), at which one 90-minute run epoch takes 79 minutes and the whole dandiset 288 hours, far beyond the 30-minute limit, before any spike detection or decoding. The claim needs the clusterless state space decoder, run on spikes detected above 100 uV from the raw broadband of every CA1 tetrode for whole sessions. The electrode table also gives every channel's location as None, so the CA1 cell-layer tetrodes and the corpus callosum reference tetrode the Methods use cannot be identified.

outcomes.statement: In a Poisson GLM over all search trials, being the previous goal roughly doubles an arm's replay rate, the strongest effect; the past arm is consistently replayed less; the future arm has a small increase significant in three of four subjects.

The notebook measures 8.8 MB/s when streaming it (data check), at which one 90-minute run epoch takes 79 minutes and the whole dandiset 288 hours, far beyond the 30-minute limit, before any spike detection or decoding. The criterion compares the visit decay with the replay enrichment of fig6a-pg-replay-persists, which needs ripples and decoding, so the claim is blocked with it. Its behavioural half was computed after the first verification round. Per block 1 to 8, goal-arm visits from 40 trials before to 40 after the last rewarded trial, against arms never a goal in the session, with a rank-sum test per trial at 0.05/80 and 0.05/81. The goal arm is visited on 0.84 to 0.90 of trial +1 (the closing trial of a completed block, the next trial of the same block for the open last block of a session), 0.33 to 0.48 of +2 and 0.23 to 0.26 of +3, against 0.06 to 0.12 for never-goal arms. With the tie-corrected test (scipy mannwhitneyu), the last trial after 0 with the goal significantly above is +2 or +3 in jaq, despereaux and montague, within both bounds (+3 and +5), under every session reading and with completed blocks only. In roquefort it is +29, a single late trial (9 of 39 goal traces against 8 of 170, p = 1.6e-4), so the behavioural half fails there. Trial +29 stands alone (+28 and +30 have p = 0.74 and 0.45, and no other trial from +20 to +40 is below 6.7e-3), and its 9 goal visits come from 9 sessions, all in a later block, none rewarded and none made while the arm was the goal again. Without tie correction (scipy ranksums) +29 gives p = 0.074 and every subject ends at +2. The claims file does not say which form, and the question asked is open. Matlab's ranksum, which the paper's code would use, corrects for ties for large samples, so the tie-corrected form is likely the code's; the outcome is blocked under either form. No trial after 0 has the goal significantly below the never-goal arms. Goal traces are 94, 95, 112 and 169 under reading (a), against 89, 85, 104 and 161 goal arms in the legend.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds the raw 30 kHz broadband, port events, position and task logs, but none of the derived data the paper's findings rest on: no spike times or waveform features, LFP, ripple or multiunit event times, linearised position or decoder output. 31 of the paper's 33 claims need ripples or clusterless decoding recomputed from about 9.1 TB of raw data, which cannot be streamed within the registry's limits.

The electrode table gives the location of all 128 channels as None in every file, so the CA1 cell-layer tetrodes used for ripple detection and decoding, and the corpus callosum tetrode used as LFP reference, cannot be identified from the data.

The files do not mark which run sessions the paper analysed. They hold 27, 32, 24 and 33 run epochs for jaq, roquefort, despereaux and montague, where the paper used 26 (24 after excluding sessions 1 and 3 of subject 1), 32, 23 and 33, and the excluded sessions are named only by number. Which jaq and despereaux epoch the paper did not count cannot be told: possible ones are jaq day 7 epoch 2 (6 rewards in 74 valid trials, no outerreps printed) and the epochs shorter than the Methods' 45 minutes (jaq day 6 epoch 4 and day 9 epoch 6, despereaux day 4 epoch 4). The paper's code repository (LorenFrankLab/Gillespie_Neuron_2021) holds a saved filter output with per-animal epoch lists that may identify them; it was not used here.

55 of the draft version's 57 files differ in content (SHA-256) from the published version's; their draft assets were modified in February and March 2022. In the file compared (montague day 4), written as NWB 2.4.0 on 2022-01-14, the DIO timestamps agree with the published version to within a microsecond, but the draft's position timestamps are shifted by about -1.59e9 s and no longer share the DIO clock; in the published version they do. The README of the paper's code links the draft.

Position is sampled at 32.9 to 33.0 Hz, where the Methods state 30 Hz, and 110 of 116 run epochs end with 1 to 4 NaN position timestamps (all of them the last samples of the series, none elsewhere); two epochs have non-increasing timestamps (up to 200).

In montague day 16 epoch 2 the StateScript log's clock steps by about 3.4 s twice against the DIO pump times early in the epoch, and in jaq day 6 epoch 4 the DIO holds one more reward pump (arm 8) 226 s after the last logged reward and 40 s after the last logged trial, so that log appears to end before the epoch. Elsewhere the log and the DIO agree to a few milliseconds and on every reward.

The task logs (StateScript, embedded as text in processing/associated_files) are the only record of the goal arm, trial structure and timeouts; there is no trials table. Five run epochs carry the log without the Python observer header that states the task parameters (rewards per goal, forage assist); for these, forage assist can be ruled out only from the log lines (no CURRENTGOAL line names more than one arm).

entries.name: 000115-gillespie-2021
entries.title: Hippocampal replay and the eight-arm goal task (Gillespie et al. 2021)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Gillespie et al. (2021) on dandiset 000115, which holds the raw CA1 tetrode broadband, port events, position and task logs of four rats in an eight-arm win-stay lose-switch task. Trials, goal blocks and reward rates are rebuilt from the task logs and checked against the hardware events. The replay findings need ripples and a clusterless decoder run on about 9.1 TB of raw data, which the dandiset holds in no reduced form.
